IATA Baggage Guidelines for Airlines: Interline Considerations on Baggage Standards (2024)

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION
The International Air Transport Association (IATA) provides comprehensive guidance to airlines on baggage policies and handling standards. This document outlines interline considerations for baggage across all participating carriers.

SECTION 2: BAGGAGE POLICY BASICS
Airlines must establish clear baggage policies that comply with IATA standards and local regulations. Policies should cover:
- Free baggage allowance
- Excess baggage charges
- Prohibited items
- Baggage tracking procedures

SECTION 3: BAGGAGE ALLOWANCE CONCEPTS
There are two standard free baggage allowance concepts:

3.1 Weight Concept
- Measured by total weight of checked-in baggage
- Typically 20kg, 23kg, 32kg, or 45kg per piece or total
- Must be clearly displayed on the ticket (weight concept)

3.2 Piece Concept
- Measured by number of pieces of checked-in baggage
- Typically 1, 2, or 3 pieces
- Must be clearly displayed on the ticket (PC notation)
- Dimensions typically 55x40x20cm or 62x45x25cm

3.3 Combined Concepts
- Some carriers combine weight and piece concepts
- Example: 2 pieces not exceeding 32kg total
- Carrier policies must be disclosed via ATPCO to all GDS systems

SECTION 4: MOST SIGNIFICANT CARRIER (MSC)
Per IATA Resolution 302, the MSC is determined as follows:

4.1 Traffic Areas
- TC1: Western Hemisphere (Americas and Caribbean)
- TC2: Europe, Middle East, and Africa
- TC3: Asia and Asia Pacific

4.2 MSC Determination Rules
- MSC = carrier on first sector crossing from one area to another
- For TC1/TC2 journeys: carrier on first sector crossing TC1 and TC2
- For multi-area journeys: apply area crossing rules in sequence

4.3 Code-share Considerations
- Marketing carrier's baggage policy prevails unless stipulated otherwise
- Operating carrier must honor MSC baggage entitlement
- Exception fares may alter MSC determination

SECTION 5: EXCESS BAGGAGE
Excess baggage is baggage beyond the free allowance.

5.1 EMD-A Documents
- Electronic Miscellaneous Document (EMD) Ancillary (EMD-A) is standard
- Reason For Issuance Code: 'C' for Baggage
- EMD-A must reference baggage details and charges

5.2 Reservation Procedures
- Create SSR XBAG in PNR for interline notification
- Format: SSR XBAG CC NN/AMSGVA 0345M15NOV.5PIECES EACH30X25X15CM TOTL85KG
- All participating carriers must honor SSR XBAG

5.3 Legacy Procedures
- Paper Excess Baggage Tickets permitted until May 31, 2021 for legacy carriers
- All carriers now required to use EMD-A system
- Transition period ended: EMD-A mandatory for all

SECTION 6: OPERATIONAL HANDLING
All airlines must implement consistent baggage handling procedures:

6.1 Mandatory Scanning Points
- Point 1: At check-in (origin)
- Point 2: At transfer (intermediate stop)
- Point 3: At connection point (outbound scan)
- Point 4: At destination (final scan)
- IATA Resolution 753 requires scanning at all 4 points

6.2 Tag Placement
- Baggage tags must be on both sides of bag
- Agent-applied tags for checked baggage
- Proper positioning ensures scanner readability

6.3 Transfer Procedures
- Baggage must clear security at transfer point if not through-checked
- Airlines responsible for baggage from acceptance to final delivery
- Through-checked baggage remains airline responsibility

SECTION 7: MISHANDLED BAGGAGE
Mishandled baggage procedures follow strict guidelines:

7.1 Definition
- Baggage delayed, lost, or damaged in transit
- Report required within specific timeframe
- Coverage per Montreal Convention limits apply

7.2 Baggage Tracing
- SITA WorldTracer system standard
- Airlines using compatible systems must integrate
- Real-time tracking mandatory for interline scenarios

7.3 RUSH Baggage
- Mishandled baggage marked as RUSH
- Forward without charge by fastest means
- To nearest airport within baggage recovery network

7.4 Claim Processing
- Claims received within 2 years of incident
- Documentation required from passenger
- Airlines determine liability per Montreal Convention

7.5 Settlement
- When responsible carrier determined: absorbs all costs
- When unknown: shared by flown mileage (proration)
- Settlement via IATA Clearing House (ICH)

SECTION 8: PROHIBITED AND RESTRICTED ITEMS
Airlines must enforce IATA Dangerous Goods restrictions:

8.1 Prohibited in Checked Baggage
- Explosives
- Flammable liquids and solids
- Oxidizers and peroxides
- Toxic and infectious substances
- Radioactive materials
- Corrosive substances
- Lithium batteries (except exceptions)

8.2 Restricted Items
- Smaller quantities allowed with restrictions
- Passenger notification required
- Special handling procedures apply

8.3 Carry-on Restrictions
- TSA/TSB restrictions apply in U.S.
- European and international regulations vary
- Airlines responsible for enforcement

SECTION 9: BAGGAGE RIGHTS AND COMPENSATION
Under Montreal Convention (2nd Protocol):

9.1 Liability Limits
- Lost baggage: SDR 1,131 (approximately USD 1,500)
- Damage to baggage: SDR 1,131
- Delay in baggage: SDR 408 (approximately USD 540)

9.2 Proof of Loss
- Passenger must provide:
  - Boarding pass
  - Baggage tag receipt
  - Proof of damage (photos for damage claims)
  - Receipts for essential items purchased

9.3 Compensation Timeline
- Initial response: within 30 days
- Settlement: within 90 days where possible
- Interest accrual: after 90 days per local law

SECTION 10: BAGGAGE FEES AND REVENUE
Standard IATA baggage fee guidelines:

10.1 First Checked Bag
- USD 25-35 typical for domestic
- USD 40-70 typical for international
- Excess baggage: per-pound or per-piece charges

10.2 Special Services
- Oversized baggage: surcharges apply
- Equipment/sports equipment: special handling fees
- Sporting goods: standard excess charges

10.3 Baggage Policies Disclosure
- Must publish in GDS (ATPCO)
- Website display required
- Staff training mandatory

SECTION 11: BEST PRACTICES FOR CUSTOMER SERVICE
Airlines should implement these practices:

11.1 Communication
- Clear policy messaging at all touchpoints
- Website, airport signage, during booking
- Multilingual support for international passengers

11.2 Exception Handling
- Authority to waive fees in hardship cases
- Escalation procedures for disputes
- Customer recovery programs

11.3 Technology Integration
- Real-time baggage tracking systems
- Mobile app integration for status updates
- Proactive customer notifications

SECTION 12: REGULATORY COMPLIANCE
Airlines must comply with:

12.1 International
- Montreal Convention (2nd Protocol)
- IATA Resolutions (302, 753, etc.)
- EU261/2004 regulations (where applicable)

12.2 Regional
- TSA requirements (United States)
- EASA requirements (Europe)
- Local jurisdiction regulations

12.3 Carrier Obligations
- Document retention: 7 years minimum
- Audit trails for all transactions
- Staff training and certification

SECTION 13: SETTLEMENT AND BILLING
Per IATA guidelines:

13.1 Interline Settlement
- Straight Rate Proration (SRP) method standard
- Proration factors based on flight segments
- Settlement through IATA Clearing House

13.2 Billing Procedures
- Invoices issued monthly
- Payment terms: 30 days standard
- Reconciliation processes defined

13.3 Dispute Resolution
- IATA mediation available
- Bilateral negotiation process
- Escalation to IATA dispute committee

APPENDIX A: KEY ACRONYMS
- MSC: Most Significant Carrier
- EMD-A: Electronic Miscellaneous Document Ancillary
- SSR XBAG: Special Service Request for Extra Baggage
- SITA: Société Internationale de Télécommunications Aéronautiques
- ATPCO: Airline Tariff Publishing Company
- GDS: Global Distribution System
- TC1/TC2/TC3: Traffic Areas 1, 2, 3
- SDR: Special Drawing Right (IMF currency)

APPENDIX B: QUICK REFERENCE CHECKLIST
- Baggage allowance clearly communicated
- MSC determined per Resolution 302
- EMD-A system implemented for excess baggage
- Scanning at all 4 mandatory points
- SITA WorldTracer or compatible system in use
- Montreal Convention limits implemented
- Staff trained on current policies
- Customer service procedures established
- Policies available in GDS
- Annual policy review scheduled

END OF DOCUMENT
